curation.canonicalNameEvidence: We present LayerWiseBench, a benchmark organized around three core concepts, layer attribution, layer binding, and visibility ordering, that structure its chart-understanding and chart-editing evaluations.
curation.decisionReason: LayerWiseBench is a formally named benchmark with a clear task, scoring metrics, and a reusable dataset and evaluation protocol.

evaluationEvidence.reuse: Generated from executable chart programs, LayerWiseBench pairs each rendered chart with spatially aligned per-layer RGBA assets and construction-derived labels for functional roles, semantic bindings, and visibility relations. From this layer-wise representation, we derive controlled understanding questions, editing targets, reference images, and evaluation regions.
evaluationEvidence.scoring: It contains 2,800 source charts across 14 chart paradigms, from which we derive 7,329 layer-wise understanding questions and 53,791 instruction-guided editing variants. Among the evaluated VLMs, Qwen3.5-27B, which achieves the highest QA macro-average, obtains 93.04% accuracy on layer attribution and 97.46% on layer binding, but only 61.46% on visibility ordering. Across the four evaluated image editors, overall mIoU ranges from 1.49% to 4.93%, and visibility-constrained edits have the lowest mIoU for every editor, ranging from 0.37% to 2.00%.
